OCCURS integer-1 TO integer-2 TIMES DEPENDING ON data-name-1
[ { ASCENDING / DESCENDING } KEY IS { data-name-2 } ... ] ... [ INDEXED BY { index-name-1 } ... ]
findings.markdown_says:
╭              ╮ KEY
       │              │
<u>OCCURS</u> │ integer-1 <u>TO</u> │ integer-2 TIMES <u>DEPENDING</u> ON data-name-1
       │              │
┌      │ <u>ASCENDING</u>    │                      ┐
│      ┤              ├ IS { data-name-2 } … │ … [ <u>INDEXED</u> BY { index-name-1 } … ]
└      ╰ <u>DESCENDING</u>   ╯                      ┘
findings.explanation: The Format 2 diagram is garbled. The printed format has a plain first line 'OCCURS integer-1 TO integer-2 TIMES DEPENDING ON data-name-1' and, on a second line, an optional bracket holding the {ASCENDING/DESCENDING} brace followed by 'KEY IS { data-name-2 } ...' (exactly as in Format 1). The markdown merges the two lines: it draws one brace spanning 'integer-1 TO', ASCENDING and DESCENDING (making 'integer-1 TO' read as an alternative of a brace shared with ASCENDING/DESCENDING), and moves the keyword KEY out of the KEY IS phrase to the top right of that brace, leaving the phrase as 'IS { data-name-2 } ...'. The bracket's left edge also falls outside the brace rather than enclosing only the ASCENDING/DESCENDING KEY IS phrase. No choice indicators are printed on this format, so none were lost.
findings.why_it_matters: A grammar or reader working from the markdown would see 'integer-1 TO' as an alternative to ASCENDING/DESCENDING and a KEY-less 'IS { data-name-2 }' phrase, so it could reject the legal source 'OCCURS 1 TO 10 TIMES DEPENDING ON N ASCENDING KEY IS K' or accept malformed variants.
